title: StoryHearth – Personalised storybooks starring your family
page_key: 127.0.0.1:8765/ | Your family's stories, bound for generations.

output.observation: The StoryHearth home page introduces a service that creates personalised illustrated storybooks using family members and memories. It explains a three-step process, offers “Proceed” and “See pricing” controls, and provides a visible “Log in” button.
output.think_aloud: This looks like what I need, but the main paragraph is difficult. Words like “multimodal generative narrative engine,” “synthesise,” and “lived-experience corpus” are not clear to me. The three steps make sense, and I can see that the digital preview is free, but I want to log in before I make my story.

site_model.what_it_is: A website for creating personalised, illustrated family storybooks.
site_model.who_it_is_for: Parents and families who want a story starring their child and another loved one.
site_model.value_proposition: Turn a family memory into an illustrated storybook, with a free digital preview and an option to print hardcovers.
main_tasks: Enter a child and another character
Share a family memory, place, and treasured object
Check the price of a printed hardcover
site_model.pricing_model: The digital preview is described as free. Printed hardcovers are available, but no price is shown on this page.
trust_signals: The company name and copyright are shown.
A UK delivery statement is shown.
There is a visible privacy link and contact email.
site_model.fit_for_me: It may be relevant because I want a story for Linh that includes our family and the lantern festival memory. I need simple language, careful cultural details, and a clear hardcover price.

page_review.purpose: Introduce the personalised storybook service and direct the visitor to start a story, view prices, or log in.
page_review.what_is_happening: The page displays the StoryHearth name, navigation links, a headline, a difficult-to-read description, two main calls to action, a free-preview and UK-shipping statement, an image, and the beginning of a three-step process.
page_review.first_impression: The service seems useful, and the steps are easy to understand, but the main description sounds more technical than a family website. I do not know what “multimodal generative narrative engine” means.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I would try to log in now because I already have an account and want to begin my story.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, I noticed the dark “Log in” button at the top right.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Yes. “Log in” clearly says that I should use my existing account.

issues.title: The main description uses difficult technical words
issues.evidence: “Leverage our multimodal generative narrative engine to synthesise bespoke, heirloom-grade story artefacts from your household's lived-experience corpus.”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I only have intermediate English, and these long technical words make me work before I understand what the service does.
issues.fix: Replace this with simple language, such as: “Turn a special family memory into a personal storybook starring your child and someone you love.”

issues.title: The hero image has no description
issues.evidence: [image (no description) 430x440]
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I cannot understand whether the image is an example of the finished book or just decoration.
issues.fix: Add meaningful alternative text, such as “Example pages from a personalised illustrated family storybook.”

issues.title: The initial price information is not enough to judge the service
issues.evidence: “Free digital preview · Printed hardcovers shipped across the UK”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I know the preview is free, but I do not yet know what a printed hardcover costs or whether there are extra charges.
issues.fix: Show a clear starting hardcover price, delivery information, and any optional costs near the “See pricing” button.

positives: The “Log in” button is easy to find.
The three-step process is clear and useful.
The page says the digital preview is free.
The site explains that printed hardcovers are shipped across the UK.
The page has privacy and contact links.

output.memory_note: The digital preview is free; the homepage does not show the hardcover price.
output.plan: I will click the visible “Log in” button and use the account details provided for this study. Then I will create the story with Linh and Bà Nội, read every page carefully, and check the hardcover price without paying.

title: Log in – StoryHearth

output.observation: The login page asks for my email address and password so I can access my StoryHearth account. It also has links for creating an account, pricing, privacy, terms, and contact.
output.think_aloud: This is simple and I understand it. I can see Email and Password inside the boxes. I will enter the account details and press “Log in.”
output.last_action_feedback: yes — the site clearly showed the result of my last action by opening the login page.

page_review.purpose: Let an existing customer enter their account.
page_review.what_is_happening: The page shows a login form with empty email and password fields, a “Log in” button, and links for new customers and website information.
page_review.first_impression: It looks calm and easy. I know exactly what to enter, although the form fields do not have proper visible labels.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I would enter my email and password now.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the Email and Password fields and the orange “Log in” button are easy to notice.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Yes. The placeholders and button tell me that I should log in to my account.

issues.title: Email and password fields have no proper labels
issues.evidence: [5] and [6] are described as “textbox (no label)” and only show the placeholders “Email” and “Password.”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I can understand the boxes now, but labelled fields are clearer and easier to use with assistive technology.
issues.fix: Add permanent visible labels for “Email address” and “Password,” and connect each label properly to its textbox.

issues.title: Footer links have very low contrast
issues.evidence: The footer text “Privacy,” “Terms,” and “Contact” is shown in very pale grey on a nearly white background.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: The words are difficult for me to read.
issues.fix: Use a darker text colour that meets accessible contrast requirements.

positives: The heading “Welcome back” clearly tells me what page this is.
The login button is large and easy to find.
The page looks simple and is not crowded with extra choices.

output.memory_note: My StoryHearth account uses the email and password provided in the study.

output.observation: The account dashboard shows that login worked, but also displays the technical warning “Error 0x80070057: profile sync incomplete.” It says “You have no books yet” and offers the orange button “+ Create a new book.”

output.last_action_feedback: partly - the new dashboard and the words “Welcome back, Demo” show that login worked, but the unexplained profile-sync error makes the result feel incomplete.

page_review.purpose: This is the account page where a customer can see saved books, create a new book, or log out.
page_review.what_is_happening: The page shows an empty library, a profile-sync error, and a link for creating a new personalised book.
page_review.first_impression: The main button is easy to notice and the empty-library message is clear, but the technical error at the top worries me.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I want to make a story for Linh now.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, I notice the large orange “+ Create a new book” button.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Yes. It clearly says that I can create a new book, although I still need to learn what information it will ask for.

issues.title: Unclear technical error
issues.evidence: “Error 0x80070057: profile sync incomplete.”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I cannot tell whether my family details are safe, whether the book will work, or what I should do to fix it.
issues.fix: Replace the code with a plain-language message such as “Your profile has not finished syncing. You can still create a book, but your latest details may be missing,” and provide a clear Try again button.

issues.title: Dashboard uses the account name instead of my name
issues.evidence: “Welcome back, Demo”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: It feels less personal and makes me check that I am in the correct account.
issues.fix: Use the customer's account display name, such as “Welcome back, Minh,” or show the account email.

issues.title: Footer links have very low contrast
issues.evidence: “Privacy”, “Terms”, and “Contact” appear very pale grey in the footer.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I can hardly read these links, and I may not notice privacy or help information.
issues.fix: Use a darker text colour with a WCAG contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 and make the clickable areas large enough.

positives: The “My books” page confirms that I am logged in.
“You have no books yet” clearly explains why the list is empty.
The main creation button is large, contrasting, and easy to find.
page_review.abandon_reason: The technical warning worries me, but the clear creation button lets me continue.

output.memory_note: The dashboard showed an unexplained “profile sync incomplete” warning after login.

page_review.purpose: Collect information about the child who will be the main character and one other person in the story.

issues.fix: Use a more neutral example such as “e.g. Bà Nội” or “e.g. Grandma Maria.”

issues.fix: Add a short optional field for a more exact relationship, or explain that the selected relationship will be used in the story.

The form is grouped into child details and other-character details.
The fields have understandable labels, and the “Next” button is easy to find.

title: Create your book – StoryHearth

output.observation: The page asks me to choose a reading level and illustration style for the book. “Lexile 200L–500L” and “Watercolour — soft and dreamy” are already selected, and I can change the choices or continue with “Next.”
output.think_aloud: The picture choices are easy to understand, but I do not know what “Lexile” means. The selected 200L–500L level might be right for a four-year-old, but I cannot be sure. I will keep the watercolour style and press “Next.”
output.last_action_feedback: partly — the new reading and illustration choices appeared, so my “Next” action worked, but the website did not warn me that the end of my story memory had been cut off.

page_review.purpose: Choose the intended reading difficulty and visual style for the personalised book.
page_review.what_is_happening: Four reading-level radio buttons and three illustration-style radio buttons are shown. The middle reading level and watercolour style are selected. There are Back and Next buttons.
page_review.first_impression: The page looks calm and the illustration choices are clear, but “Lexile” is a technical word. I do not know which reading range is correct for Linh.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes. The style choices are easy, but I would want a simple explanation before choosing a Lexile range.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes. I can see the reading-level radio buttons, illustration-style radio buttons, and the orange “Next” button.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Partly. The illustration labels clearly describe the appearance, but the Lexile labels do not explain whether they are easy, medium, or hard for a child.

issues.title: Reading-level choices use an unexplained technical scale
issues.evidence: The heading says “Reading level,” but the options say “Lexile BR–200L,” “Lexile 200L–500L,” “Lexile 500L–800L,” and “Lexile 800L+.”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I do not know what Lexile means, so I cannot confidently choose the right level for Linh, who is four.
issues.fix: Add a plain-English explanation and child-friendly labels, such as “Age 4–6 — Lexile BR–200L,” “Age 7–12 — Lexile 200L–500L,” and a short sentence explaining what Lexile measures.

issues.title: The preselected reading level is not explained
issues.evidence: [22] radio “Lexile 200L–500L” (checked)
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I worry the preselected range may be too difficult for my daughter, and I do not know why it was selected for me.
issues.fix: Preselect a level based on Linh’s entered age, and show a note such as “Selected from Linh’s age: 4.” Ask me to confirm it.

positives: The page has a clear heading and groups the choices under simple labels.
The currently selected options are visible.
The illustration descriptions are warm and easy to compare.
The Back and Next buttons make my next choice clear.

new_issues.title: Story text was silently cut off after 200 characters
new_issues.evidence: The previous field “Tell us the memory or idea behind your story” showed “200 characters” and the end of the memory disappeared after “they float the lantern”.
new_issues.why_it_matters_to_me: The important action of floating the lantern on the river was lost. The website accepted the form without telling me that my family memory was incomplete.
new_issues.fix: Show the remaining character count before the limit, allow a longer story, and do not continue until the text fits. If text is removed, show a clear warning beside the field and let me edit it.

output.memory_note: The website selected “Lexile 200L–500L” and “Watercolour — soft and dreamy” by default.
output.plan: I will keep the selected watercolour style and press “Next” because it is an easy choice. I am not fully sure about the Lexile range, so I will check the generated text carefully and use Back if the reading level is clearly wrong.
